cues.say: Component 21: Safe deploys. Release new code to a few users first, keep a tested way back, and stop releasing around the event. You'll bring this up during go-live prep.
Think of it as: Taste the soup before serving the whole room. Use it for any release near the event.
Here's a real scenario. Wednesday before the snowy weekend: the tire shop ships a bug fix.
Without it: The fix goes to 100% at once.
A bad release breaks booking for everyone.
With it: Canary: 5% of traffic gets the new version.
Errors on that 5% jump from 0.1% to 4%: one-click rollback.
Proper fix Thursday morning, then freeze until Monday.
Why it works: Most outages come from changes. A canary limits who, a rollback limits how long, a freeze removes the risk.
In the interview, say: Nothing ships during the window.
A few related terms you may hear.
Canary: New version to 1 to 5% of users first.
Rollback: A tested, one-step return to the last version.
Code freeze: No releases around the event.
Rolling deploy: Replace copies a few at a time; can kill work in progress.
Blue-green: Old and new side by side; switch all traffic at once.
